narrative.overview:
Consumit feels cinematic, editorial, and human: a near-black room lit by warm ivory type and rare signals of color. The interface is intimate rather than glossy, with enough quiet space for artwork, taste, and other people’s perspectives to carry emotional weight.

The system pairs decisive controls with restrained surfaces. It should feel alive with other people’s taste without becoming noisy, gamified, or generically “streaming app.” Generic dashboards and glossy-tech decoration are explicit anti-references.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black, flat surfaces with warm editorial contrast
Charter display type paired with compact DejaVu Sans controls
Rare orange action signals with semantically reserved lilac and lime
Purposeful composition that becomes distinct on mobile

rules.name: The Scarce Signal Rule
rules.body: Orange communicates brand, selection, progress, or commitment; it is never ambient decoration.

rules.name: The Semantic Accent Rule
rules.body: Lilac means social or taste context, and lime means presence or health. Do not swap their jobs for variety.

rules.name: The Operational Status Rule
rules.body: Orange marks selection, commitment, and progress; Warm Copy marks checking or slow states; Positive Lime means healthy or present.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Serif type tells the story; sans-serif type helps the member act.

rules.name: The Flat Interface Rule
rules.body: Shadows may separate artwork, but ordinary controls and content panels remain flat.

rules.name: The Perceptible Control Rule
rules.body: Interactive boundaries use the dedicated control outline and keep a minimum 44px target; faint separators only divide passive content.

rules.name: The Human Signal Rule
rules.body: Presence, save state, status, rank, and compatibility are expressed in text as well as color or iconography.

rules.name: The Artwork Leads Rule
rules.body: Supplied artwork preserves its intended aspect ratio and leads media compositions; gradients exist only to protect artwork legibility.

rules.name: The Social Context Rule
rules.body: Taste and social components explain why content matters through named people and readable context rather than anonymous engagement totals.

rules.name: The Home Cadence Rule
rules.body: Preserve Home’s shipped section order and alternation of cinematic, social, utility, and editorial beats; do not generalize that composition to other pages.

rules.name: The Rank Behind the Poster Rule
rules.body: A Trending Card’s oversized rank sits behind the poster at its vertical center; never float it above the artwork or reduce it to an ordinary corner badge.

rules.name: The Human Reason Rule
rules.body: Profile and taste surfaces explain affinity through named people, shared worlds, and readable reasons; totals never stand alone as proof.

rules.name: The Single Promise Rule
rules.body: A title masthead sells one film or series; continuation state, member evidence, and secondary actions clarify the decision without becoming rival heroes.

rules.name: The State, Evidence, Action Rule
rules.body: Episode, library, and ordered-list rows keep current state, supporting evidence, and the available action visibly distinct.

rules.name: The Reduced Shell Rule
rules.body: Authentication, onboarding, report, and watch flows remove unrelated global navigation while retaining exact brand identity, clear escape routes, and the context needed to finish the job.

rules.name: The Player Ownership Rule
rules.body: Consumit owns the playback controls and media surface; providers supply authorized direct media through an adapter boundary and never replace the interface with an embed.

rules.name: The Synchronized Watch State Rule
rules.body: Source selection, watch status, player status, and active detail always describe the same application state.

rules.name: The Social Boundary Rule
rules.body: Follow and Circle support asynchronous discovery; direct or private member messaging is not part of the product.

rules.name: The Honest Recovery Rule
rules.body: Empty, loading, and error states name the affected content, its impact, and the next available recovery without implying data loss that did not occur.

dos: Do use the supplied brand and artwork assets instead of recreating them with generic icons.
Do reserve ivory for confident immediate actions and orange for committed progression.
Do preserve visible keyboard focus, touch-safe control heights, and readable metadata contrast.
Do finish each shared component and its states before composing the next screen.
Do keep Home’s section order and responsive discovery rails specific to Home.
Do keep playback selection, header status, player status, and active source detail synchronized from one application state.
Do explain empty, loading, and error states in terms of member impact and the next useful recovery.
donts: Don't introduce large pills, routine gradients, glass effects, or floating dashboard cards.
Don't use orange, lilac, or lime as interchangeable decoration.
Don't reduce every surface to a rounded card grid.
Don't treat mobile as a scaled-down desktop composition.
Don't reuse Home’s editorial cadence as a universal page template.
Don't synthesize the Consumit mark with styled text in reduced branded headers or hide onboarding skip on mobile.
Don't put provider ranking, health, entitlement, streaming-adapter, or switching logic inside Component 17, and don't introduce iframe or embed playback.
Don't add private or direct messaging actions to member profiles or suggestions.
